findings.title: Add-Shift sheet defaults to the Night type even when Night is switched off — sheet and hero pay a differential the lab prices at base
findings.detail: AddShiftSheet initialises `shiftType` to the literal `'night'` and never reconciles it with the `active` list it renders chips from. Settings lets a nurse toggle any differential off (`tog`, index.html:4690). When Night is inactive: no SHIFT TYPE chip is highlighted (the chip row only maps `active`), yet `previewGross` is still `shiftGross(baseRate, differentials['night'], draft)` — `hourlyRate` (1119-1124) never looks at `active` — so the preview prices a Night shift, and the primary button on a fresh day commits `draftShift()` with `shiftType:'night'`. The hero then prices that shift with the Night differential too. The pattern lab's Night brush goes through `patternCellShiftType`, which resolves to `'base'` when `night.active` is false. Numbers from the real functions (base $65.15, defaults, Night off): sheet preview +$902 gross / +$702 take-home; two such shifts → hero $1,404; the same two nights in a 7-day pattern → lab $1,217 (per shift $781.80 vs $901.80). The sheet is the wrong one: it silently selects a type the nurse turned off, with no chip lit to show why. (If she *deletes* Night instead, `differentials['night']` is undefined and all three surfaces fall back to base — dollars agree, but the sheet still saves an unknown `shiftType` key.)
findings.failure: Nurse deactivates Night in Settings ("I only work days"), taps a calendar day, sees no shift-type chip selected but a preview of +$902 gross / +$702 take-home, taps "Add shift". Her calendar and hero now carry a Night-differential shift she cannot see a reason for; the pattern lab, given the same rotation, shows $187 less per paycheck than the hero.
findings.fix: Initialise from the active list: `useState(()=> (Object.entries(differentials).find(([k,d])=>d.active && k!=='overtime')||['base'])[0])`, and add a small effect that resets `shiftType` to that value whenever the current `shiftType` is no longer in `active` (covers a Settings change while the sheet is open). No wage-core function changes; add a harness assertion: deactivate Night, open the sheet, assert a chip is highlighted and the preview equals `shiftGross(base, differentials[thatChip], ...)`.

findings.title: Per-shift preview, calendar day amounts and goal counts use a flat keep-ratio that ignores per-paycheck deductions the hero and pattern lab subtract
findings.where: index.html:2819-2820 (`ficaForPreview`/`keepRatio`); consumers 4105 (`previewNet`), 3919 + 3933 (calendar `t.g*keepRatio`), 4747 (Settings goals `baseRate*12*keepRatio`), 3434/3512 (`sampleWeekendNet` "Pick up a weekend night?"); vs 1231-1255 `computeNet`
findings.detail: `keepRatio = 1 - (federal+state+fica)/100` is applied to gross. `computeNet` (used by the hero via `calc` at 2787-2810 and by `patternMetrics` at 1298) additionally subtracts flat `pretaxDeductions` and `posttaxDeductions` per paycheck, reduces the income-tax base by the pre-tax amount, and applies `customWithholdings` (percent ones proportionally to income-tax base). Every user who fills DEDUCTIONS · per pay period (Settings 4736-4739, onboarding 5803-5805, or a paystub import that sets `pretaxDeductions` at 3378) gets two incompatible take-home models on screen. Ran the real functions with base $65.15, defaults, $300 pre-tax / $50 post-tax: one 12h Night — sheet says "This shift adds +$902 gross · about +$702 take-home" (implied keep 78%), hero after saving it as the only shift: $396, Keep 44%. Six such Nights: the six calendar day amounts ("~$702" each, disclaimer at 3580 says "estimated take-home") sum to $4,212; the hero says $3,906 and the pattern lab for the same Mon–Wed-nights rotation says $3,905.81 — hero and lab agree, preview/chips do not. Beyond the first shift the marginal figure happens to be right ($702.05 for the 2nd), so the model is defensible as "marginal once the paycheck covers the flat deductions" — but the copy is "This shift adds", and on an empty period it is $306 high. Percent-type `customWithholdings` (reachable only via Settings → Import JSON, there is no editor) are a straight omission: a 6% percent withholding makes the hero's marginal $648 while the preview still says $702. The hero/lab are right; the keepRatio surfaces are wrong.
findings.failure: A nurse with a $300/paycheck 403b and $50 union dues opens the first day of a new pay period: the sheet promises +$702 take-home; she taps Add and the hero shows $396. Later, adding up the ~$ amounts on her six calendar days gives $4,212 against a hero of $3,906 — the day figures never reconcile with the paycheck they sit under.
findings.fix: Derive the sheet's figure from the hero's own model as a true marginal: in App compute `marginalNetFor = g => computeNet(calc.gross+g, taxInputs).net - calc.net` (calc already scopes to the active period) and pass it instead of `keepRatio` for the sheet when the day is in the active period; for the calendar day chips and goals either use the same marginal or, if the per-shift 'gross × keep' framing is deliberate, fold percent custom withholdings into `keepRatio` and change the chip disclaimer to "before your $X per-paycheck deductions". Does not edit shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet/calc/statOf/patternMetrics, but every option changes a displayed dollar figure, so run it under the wage-core skill (baseline probes + hero/breakdown equality against the deployed build) and add a probe: with pretax>0, preview for the first shift of an empty period must equal `computeNet(g,t).net`.

findings.title: Pattern lab labels a multi-paycheck average as "Take-home per paycheck" — for the shipped 4 on / 4 off preset no real paycheck matches the number
findings.where: index.html:1257-1301 `patternMetrics` (span = lcm(n,14), `periodGross = gross/periods`, `periodNet = computeNet(periodGross)`), labels at 4540 ("Take-home per paycheck"), 4447 ("/ paycheck"), 4428 ("Take-home / paycheck"); preset at 1160-1161
findings.detail: For a cycle that does not divide 14 (the 8-day 4on4off preset, 28-day, any custom length) `patternMetrics` averages gross over lcm(n,14) days and runs `computeNet` once on that averaged gross. The UI presents the result with no 'average' qualifier, and the preset blurb warns only that days "drift across the week". Ran the real functions (base $65.15, defaults) on the 4on4off preset anchored 2026-09-14: lab shows $5,036 per paycheck (84 hrs). Pricing the same rotation the way the hero will after "Put it on the calendar" — 14-day windows at each of the 8 possible pay-period offsets — gives $4,212 (72 h), $4,914 (84 h), $5,616 or $5,677 (96 h); none equals $5,036 and the gap is −$824 to +$641. Control: the Pitman 14-day preset gives lab $4,475.29 and hero $4,475.29 at all 14 offsets, so this is specific to n∤14. Worse, with flat deductions the lab's figure is not even the honest average: with $300 pre / $50 post `computeNet(avgGross)` = $4,729 while the mean of the actual paycheck nets is $4,623 (flat deductions and the `Math.max(0,…)` clamp make computeNet non-linear). The lab is the wrong surface; the hero is pricing real paychecks.
findings.failure: Nurse picks "4 on, 4 off nights", reads "$5,036 take-home per paycheck", puts it on the calendar, and the hero for the current period shows $4,212. She reports "the number looks wrong" — and whichever period she scrolls to, none shows $5,036.
findings.fix: In `patternMetrics`, price each 14-day window across the span (offsets 0..n−1 for n∤14, one window when n | 14), collect `computeNet(windowGross,taxes).net` per window, and return `periodNet` = mean of those nets plus `periodNetMin`/`periodNetMax`; the lab shows "avg $X per paycheck · ranges $A–$B" (and the comparison table uses the mean). This changes a displayed dollar figure and edits `patternMetrics` — Invariant 3, dedicated session, probe that n=7/14 results are byte-identical to today and that the 4on4off mean equals the mean of the 8 offset windows. Cheap interim: when `n%14!==0` change the labels to "average per paycheck" and add a line to the preset blurb.

findings.title: Hero's "Taxes & deductions" chip and the Breakdown rows disagree on the same paycheck when gross is below the flat deductions
findings.where: index.html:3487 (chip prints `calc.ded`) vs 3981-3987 + 4003-4006 (Breakdown rows print display-capped `calc.pre`/`calc.post`); caps computed at 1248-1251 in `computeNet`
findings.detail: `computeNet` deliberately caps the *displayed* pre/post rows so Breakdown sums to gross, but the hero chip prints the uncapped `ded`. Ran the real function: one 4h base shift with $300 pre-tax / $50 post-tax → hero chips read "Gross $261 · Taxes & deductions –$370 · Keep 0%", take-home $0; Breakdown for the identical `calc` shows Pre-tax $241 + FICA $20 = $261 (post-tax row hidden). Two totals for one paycheck, on adjacent surfaces. The chip is the wrong one — a paycheck cannot deduct more than its gross, which is the whole reason the caps exist. Common at period start (first short shift of a fortnight) and in the sample/rough estimate paths.
findings.failure: On a pay period holding one short shift the hero says her deductions ($370) exceed her gross ($261); tapping the breakdown shows deductions of $261. Which one does she believe?
findings.fix: Print `fmt(calc.gross - calc.net)` in the chip (equals the capped rows' sum; identical to `calc.ded` whenever gross covers the deductions, so no other surface changes). Pure render change, no wage-core edit; add a smoke assertion that chip and Breakdown totals agree for a gross-below-deductions seed.

findings.title: Add-Shift preview, calendar day cells, goal lines and the weekend-night card use a keep-ratio that omits percent custom withholdings, so they disagree with the hero and the pattern lab
findings.where: index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio) -> consumers at 4104-4105 & 4245-4248 (AddShiftSheet preview + goal line), 3919 & 3933 (Calendar day cell), 4747 (Settings '≈ N typical 12h shifts'), 3434 & 3512 ('Pick up a weekend night?' card)
findings.detail: The hero (calc, 2787-2810) and the pattern lab (patternMetrics 1298) both price take-home through computeNet(), which subtracts customWithholdings — including type:'percent' ones computed on incomeTaxBase (1243). Every other take-home figure in the app is previewGross*keepRatio, and keepRatio = 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview)/100 knows nothing about customWithholdings. Omitting the flat per-period deductions from a per-shift marginal figure is defensible; omitting a percent withholding is not — it is a per-dollar rate that applies fully at the margin. Reproduced with the extracted functions: base $50, fed 12, state 2.5, standard FICA, one custom withholding {Pension, 5, percent}, one 12h base shift in the period -> hero net 437.10 (Keep 73%), lab periodNet 437.10, Add-Shift previewNet 467 (implied keep 78%), day cell ~$467. Settings' goal line even claims to be 'the same per-shift take-home the Add-Shift preview uses' (4745-4746) — it is, and both are off from the hero. Hero and lab agree with each other; the preview family is the wrong one.
findings.failure: A nurse whose Settings carry a percent 'Other withholding' (e.g. a 5% 403b) logs one 12h day shift: the hero says $437 take-home this period and the lab says $437 / paycheck for a one-shift fortnight, but the Add-Shift sheet for that exact shift says 'about +$467 take-home', the calendar cell shows ~$467, and a $5,000 goal reads '≈ 11 typical 12h shifts' in Settings and in the preview when the hero's rate needs 12. Every pickup she evaluates is overstated by the withholding percentage.
findings.fix: Fold the percent withholdings into keepRatio at 2820: const pctCW = (customWithholdings||[]).reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+pctCW)/100). All five consumers then agree with computeNet at the margin. Add a harness assertion that, with a percent withholding set, Math.round(previewGross*keepRatio) === Math.round(computeNet(previewGross, taxInputs).net) when pretax/posttax are 0. Not an Invariant-3 function, but it changes displayed dollars, so run the wage-math probes and the deployed-build equality check.

findings.title: Add-Shift sheet defaults to shiftType 'night' even when the Night differential is switched off, pricing a differential the nurse disabled while the pattern lab prices the same Night at base
findings.where: index.html:4077 (useState('night')) vs 4099 (active chip filter) and 1206-1213 (patternCellShiftType); second instance at 3434 (sampleWeekendNet uses differentials['weekend-eve'] regardless of .active)
findings.detail: AddShiftSheet initialises shiftType to the literal 'night' and only changes it on a chip tap (4208). The chip list is filtered to active differentials (4099), so with night.active=false no chip is highlighted, yet previewGross = shiftGross(baseRate, differentials['night'], draft) still adds the night amount, and draftShift()/save (4109, 4128) file a shift with shiftType:'night'. shiftGross never consults .active, so the hero then prices it with the differential too. The pattern lab makes the opposite call: patternCellShiftType resolves a 'night' cell to 'base' when night is inactive, so a Night 12h cell is priced at base and, on apply, placed as shiftType 'base'. Reproduced: night.active=false, base $50 — sheet preview gross 720 (no chip lit), lab Night cell -> 'base', gross 600. Same class of bug at 3434: the 'Pick up a weekend night?' card prices differentials['weekend-eve'] whether or not it is active (and at base, mislabeled, if she deleted it).
findings.failure: A day-shift nurse toggles Night off in Settings. She opens Add-Shift on a Tuesday: no shift-type chip is selected, the preview reads '+$720 gross' for 12h, and tapping 'Add shift' files a Night shift (☾ glyph, purple dot) that the hero counts at base+$10/hr. The pattern lab, given a Night 12h cell on the same Tuesday, says $600 and places a Day (regular) shift. Two surfaces, same input, $120 apart; the sheet is wrong because it charges a differential she turned off and does so without showing any selection.
findings.fix: Initialise the sheet from the active list: const [shiftType,setType] = useState(()=> (differentials.night&&differentials.night.active) ? 'night' : (Object.keys(differentials).find(k=>differentials[k].active && k!=='overtime') || 'base')). Also make the weekend card (3434) fall back the way patternCellShiftType does when weekend-eve is inactive. Negative-test: with night inactive, assert the sheet opens with a highlighted chip and the preview equals shiftGross for that chip. Leave shiftGross's .active-blindness for stored shifts alone — changing that is Invariant-3 work and a product call.

findings.title: Hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip shows the uncapped total, so when flat deductions exceed gross it contradicts both the $0 take-home beside it and the Breakdown rows
findings.where: index.html:3487 (chip renders calc.ded) vs 1246-1251 (computeNet caps pre/post for display) and 3980-3987 (Breakdown rows use calc.pre/calc.post)
findings.detail: computeNet returns ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw uncapped and net = max(0, gross-ded), then separately computes display-capped pre/post so the Breakdown rows sum to gross. The hero chip prints calc.ded, the Breakdown prints the capped rows. Reproduced: gross 600, pretax 800, fed 12, state 2.5, standard FICA -> hero shows 'Gross $600', 'Taxes & deductions –$846', take-home '$0'; the Breakdown for the same period shows Pre-tax –$554, FICA –$46, take-home $0 (rows sum to –$600).
findings.failure: Early in a pay period a nurse with a $300/period 401k+health pre-tax deduction has logged one 4h shift ($200 gross). The hero reads Gross $200 / Taxes & deductions –$315 / $0 take-home — figures that do not reconcile — while 'See the full breakdown' shows deductions totalling –$200. Same numbers, two different totals on adjacent screens.
findings.fix: Render the chip from the reconciled figure: –{fmt(calc.gross - calc.net)} (equivalently calc.pre+calc.fed+calc.fica+calc.st+calc.post+calc.cw) at 3487, leaving computeNet untouched. One harness assertion: with pretax > gross, the chip's number equals the sum of the Breakdown rows.

findings.title: Hero hours chip prints the raw float sum, so it can show '36.900000000000006 hrs' directly above a stat that says '36.9'
findings.where: index.html:3489 ({calc.hours} hrs · N shifts) vs 3496 (calc.hours.toFixed(calc.hours%1?1:0)) and 3970 (YearList uses toFixed)
findings.detail: calc.hours is accumulated with += over shift and PTO hours (2796, 2803). The .ics importer rounds each event to a tenth (861) but the sum of tenths is not exact in binary floating point, and NumInput (4016-4029) accepts any decimal the nurse types. The stat under the hero and the YearList both format with toFixed; the chip interpolates the number raw. Reproduced: three 12.3h shifts -> chip '36.900000000000006 hrs · 3 shifts', stat '36.9'; 12.1h + 12.2h -> '24.299999999999997 hrs'.
findings.failure: A nurse whose calendar feed lists 07:00–19:18 shifts (12.3h after the importer's rounding) sees 'Keep 73%' next to '36.900000000000006 hrs · 3 shifts' in the hero, while the 'hours this period' stat just below says 36.9.
findings.fix: Format the chip the same way as the stat: {calc.hours.toFixed(calc.hours%1?1:0)} hrs at 3489 (or round once in calc: hours = Math.round(hours*100)/100 — that touches calc, so prefer the render-side fix).

findings.title: Add-Shift preview ignores percent custom withholdings; hero and pattern lab both apply them
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio), consumed at 4104-4105 (AddShiftSheet previewNet), 4240-4244 (preview render), 3910 (calendar cell aria-label), 4747-4748 (Settings '≈ N typical 12h shifts'), 3434/3512 (weekend-night card)
findings.detail: The hero (App.calc → computeNet, 2787-2810 / 1231-1253) and the pattern lab (patternMetrics → computeNet, 1298) both subtract percent customWithholdings (computeNet line 1242: `incomeTaxBase*(amount/100)`). The Add-Shift preview prices a shift with `keepRatio = 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview)/100` (2819-2820), which has no term for customWithholdings at all. Percent withholdings are a marginal rate, so every shift the preview prices is overstated by exactly that percentage of gross. Reproduced by extracting the real functions: seed baseRate 50, fed 12%, state 4%, FICA standard, customWithholdings [{amount:5,type:'percent'}], one 12h base shift ($600 gross): hero take-home rises by $428.10, pattern lab readout for the same single-shift 14-day cycle says $428.10, Add-Shift preview says '+$458 take-home' and '≈ $38.17/hr'. The preview is the wrong one — it is the only surface not routed through the per-paycheck model. The same keepRatio feeds the Settings goal line (base×12×keepRatio), the calendar cell's 'about $X take-home' aria-label, and the dashboard 'Pick up a weekend night?' card, so all four disagree with the hero by the same factor. (Related but arguably by design: with a flat pretaxDeduction of $500 the first shift of a period raises the hero by $38.10 while the preview still says +$458; the second shift then adds $458.10 — a flat-deduction absorption effect, not a rate error.)
findings.failure: Nurse with a 5% percent-type custom withholding (403b, union dues, extra withholding) opens Add Shift on an empty day: preview reads '+$458 take-home · ≈ $38.17/hr'. She adds it and the hero take-home rises by $428. Pattern lab prices the identical shift at $428. Her goal line in Settings and the '≈N shifts' in the preview are likewise ~7% too optimistic.
findings.fix: Fold percent custom withholdings into keepRatio at 2819-2820: `const cwPct = (customWithholdings||[]).reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+cwPct)/100);` (add customWithholdings to any dependency list that memoizes it). Add a smoke assertion seeding a percent withholding and asserting previewNet === Math.round(gross*(1-(fed+state+fica+cw)/100)) and that the hero delta for one shift matches within rounding. keepRatio is not in the Invariant 3 function list, but it changes a displayed dollar figure, so follow the wage-core skill's probe + deployed-build equality protocol.

findings.title: Pattern lab 'Take-home per paycheck' is a multi-paycheck average for cycles that don't divide 14, with no cue — no actual paycheck ever matches it
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1282-1298 (patternMetrics span=lcm(n,14), periodGross=gross/periods), labels at 4540 ('Take-home per paycheck'), 4428 ('Take-home / paycheck'), 4447 ('/ paycheck ·')
findings.detail: patternMetrics averages gross over lcm(cycle,14) days and labels the result 'per paycheck'. For 7- and 14-day cycles this equals the hero exactly (verified: pitman, mtw-nights, 3-1-3-7, weekend presets, anchor 3 days off the pay-period start, messy taxes — lab === hero to the cent). For the shipped '4 on, 4 off nights' preset (cycle 8, span 56) and any 28-day or custom cycle, the number is an average of 2–4 different paychecks and the UI never says so. The only drift hint (4534-4536) talks about weekdays, and for a 28-day cycle `drifts` is false so there is no hint at all. Reproduced: 4on4off, base 50, defaults, anchor 2026-09-13, applied 8 weeks: lab says $3,967 take-home / $5,196 gross / 84 hrs; the hero shows $4,457 (96 hrs) for paychecks 1–2 and $3,477 (72 hrs) for paychecks 3–4 — the lab's figure appears on no paycheck. A front-loaded 28-day custom cycle (7 shifts in weeks 1–2, 3 in weeks 3–4): lab $2,838, hero $3,967 then $1,709 — a 40% miss on the first paycheck with `drifts:false` and no warning. Neither surface is mathematically wrong; the lab's label is, because the surface's stated purpose is 'see the paycheck it makes before you commit'.
findings.failure: Nurse picks the '4 on, 4 off nights' preset, reads 'Take-home per paycheck $3,967', taps 'Put it on the calendar', and the hero for that very period shows $4,457; two paychecks later it shows $3,477. In the side-by-side table she compares 4-on-4-off's $3,967 against Pitman's exact $3,207 as if both were single-paycheck figures.
findings.fix: In PatternLab, when `lcm(metrics.n,14) > 14` (i.e. metrics.n does not divide 14), change the label/sub-line to say it is an average — e.g. 'Take-home per paycheck (avg. over {span/14} paychecks)' at 4540 and a footnote on the 4428/4447 rows — or have patternMetrics also return the per-period min/max (loop the span in 14-day windows, run computeNet on each) and render 'between $3,477 and $4,457, avg $3,967'. Label-only change needs no wage-core session; the min/max variant touches patternMetrics and does.

findings.title: Template ('fixed') brushes never pick up weekend differentials, contradicting the grid hint; two identical-looking Saturday cells price $78 apart
findings.where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1201-1212 (patternCellShiftType: `if(cell.kind==='fixed') return cell.shiftType`), brush construction 4365-4375 (brushCell), hint 4536, cellLabel/cellColor 4318-4327
findings.detail: Generic 'day'/'night' brushes resolve to weekend-day/weekend-eve on Sat/Sun (1205-1211), but a cell painted from a saved template keeps the template's shiftType verbatim. The hint under the grid (4536) says unconditionally 'Weekend days pick up your weekend differentials automatically.' A 'Nights' template (shiftType 'night', 12h, 19:00) and the built-in Night brush produce cells with identical glyph (☾), identical colour (both `differentials['night'].color`, 4318-4322) and identical label ('Night 12h from 7:00 PM', 4323-4327), yet on a Saturday the generic one prices at weekend-eve ($798 at base 50 with defaults) and the template one at night ($720). Reproduced via patternCellShiftType on 2026-09-19: generic night → 'weekend-eve', fixed night → 'night'; generic day → 'weekend-day', fixed base → 'base'. The applied shifts carry the same type as the readout, so hero and lab agree with each other — the disagreement is between the lab's two brushes and between the lab and its own hint. The comment at 1139-1141 says fixed cells keeping their type is deliberate, but nothing in the UI tells the nurse which brush she used.
findings.failure: Nurse saves her usual 'Nights' shift as a template (the app encourages this), opens the pattern lab, paints Fri/Sat/Sun with the ⚡ Nights brush and reads 'Weekend days pick up your weekend differentials automatically.' The readout is $156/paycheck lower than if she had painted the same three cells with the built-in ☾ Night brush, and the Sat/Sun shifts land on the calendar as plain 'Night', not 'Weekend night'.
findings.fix: Either (a) in patternCellShiftType, when cell.kind==='fixed' and cell.shiftType is 'base' or 'night', apply the same weekend upgrade the generic branch does (keeps custom-*/holiday/bonus-incentive templates verbatim) — this changes applied shift types, so run the wage-core probe protocol even though the function is outside the Invariant 3 list; or (b) make the hint at 4536 conditional: only claim automatic weekend differentials when the active brush is a generic one, and mark fixed weekend cells (e.g. a different glyph or 'as template' in cellLabel) so the two brushes are distinguishable.

findings.title: 'Pick up a weekend night?' card prices weekend-eve even when that differential is switched off or deleted
findings.detail: sampleWeekendNet = shiftGross(baseRate, differentials['weekend-eve'], {shiftType:'weekend-eve',...}) * keepRatio, with no check of `.active` and no fallback when the key is absent. Settings lets a nurse toggle weekend-eve off (4712) or delete it (4716, any key but 'base'). When off, the Add-Shift sheet the card's 'Try it' button opens does not offer weekend-eve as a chip (4099 filters on active) and the pattern lab resolves a weekend night to 'night' (1208-1209), so the shift she can actually log is base+night, not base+weekend-eve — the card is the odd one out. When deleted, hourlyRate(base, undefined) returns base, so the card prices a 'weekend night' at the bare base rate. Also inherits the keepRatio omission from finding 1.
findings.failure: Nurse whose hospital pays a single night differential turns off 'Weekend night' in Settings. Dashboard still says 'Pick up a weekend night? That's about +$609 take-home' (base 50, $16.50 weekend-eve, 12h, default taxes); she taps Try it, the sheet only offers Night, and adding it raises the hero by $550.
findings.fix: At 3434 pick the shift type the way the pattern lab does: `const wkKey = differentials['weekend-eve']?.active ? 'weekend-eve' : (differentials['night']?.active ? 'night' : 'base');` and price that; hide the card (or reword it) when the resolved key is 'base'.
